blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — atorvastatin hepatic safety monitoring
stem: A client is starting atorvastatin. Which liver-enzyme monitoring plan is most consistent with current prescribing information?

options.A: Obtain liver enzymes before therapy and then every month during treatment, even when the client has no hepatic symptoms and previous results are stable.
options.B: Obtain liver enzymes before therapy and then at a fixed annual interval, because routine yearly testing is required during otherwise stable atorvastatin treatment.
options.C: Defer liver-enzyme testing at initiation and obtain it after treatment only if the client develops symptoms suggesting hepatic injury or jaundice.
options.D: Consider liver-enzyme testing before therapy and repeat it when clinically indicated rather than scheduling testing at a universal fixed interval.

rationale: Current atorvastatin prescribing information states to consider liver-enzyme testing before initiation and when clinically indicated thereafter. It does not require routine monthly or annual testing for every clinically stable client. Therefore D is the best answer. A and B impose fixed surveillance intervals not required by the label. C omits the label-supported consideration of testing before treatment begins and makes post-initiation testing entirely symptom-triggered.
educational_objective: Teach that atorvastatin labeling supports considering liver-enzyme testing before initiation and repeating testing when clinically indicated rather than using a universal fixed monitoring interval.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine); source label by Rising Pharma Holdings, Inc.; repackaged by Preferred Pharmaceuticals Inc.
source_document_title: Atorvastatin Calcium Tablets, for oral use — Prescribing Information
source_locator: Full Prescribing Information §5.3 Hepatic Dysfunction and Highlights of Prescribing Information: consider liver-enzyme testing before initiating atorvastatin and as clinically indicated thereafter; promptly discontinue for serious hepatic injury with clinical symptoms and/or hyperbilirubinemia or jaundice.
source_claim_supported: Atorvastatin labeling advises consideration of liver-enzyme testing before initiation and repeat testing when clinically indicated, not routine testing at a universal fixed interval.
blueprint_locator: Printed p. 38, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: review pertinent data prior to medication administration; educate clients about medications; evaluate client response to medication; assess for medication side/adverse effects and related laboratory findings.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices as parallel monitoring plans and removed the isolated absolute-word distractor cue.
Used plausible fixed-interval alternatives rather than obviously implausible claims while preserving one label-supported best answer.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms D uniquely matches the current §5.3 wording. A and B add unsupported universal fixed intervals, while C omits the pre-initiation testing consideration and narrows follow-up to symptoms alone. No second defensible answer or material cueing remains.
